docs.title: B3 LIMS documentation
docs.text:
B3 LIMS is an open-source system for the samples, freezers, notebooks and shipments of a research lab. It runs on one computer, on a lab server or on a cluster.

I want to... Read Install it and try it Install and upgrade Learn what each module does User guide Change a setting Configuration Run it for many people behind HTTPS Production deployment Use Slurm, PAM or Jupyter servers Clusters (optional) See what is planned Roadmap Contribute code Contributing

docs.title: The shortest path
docs.text:
pipx install "git+https://github.com/leepusp/biobank.git"
biobank-local setup --demo
biobank-local run

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and sign in with the administrator you created, or as demo (password demo-password-123) to explore the fictional demo lab. Change or remove the demo user before real use.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: biobank-local setup writes config.env in the data folder (permissions 600, it holds the secret key). Edit it and restart to change a setting. Environment variables override the file.

docs.title: Local installation (biobank.standalone_settings)
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose BIOBANK_LOCAL_ROOT ~/.biobank-local Data folder (also --root) BIOBANK_SECRET_KEY generated by setup Cryptographic signing key; keep it secret and stable BIOBANK_DATABASE_URL SQLite in the data folder e.g. postgres://user:pass@host:5432/biobank BIOBANK_ALLOWED_HOSTS localhost,127.0.0.1 Comma-separated names people use to reach the server BIOBANK_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS empty Public https:// addresses when behind a reverse proxy BIOBANK_TIME_ZONE UTC Time zone of dates shown BIOBANK_HOST 127.0.0.1 Address biobank-local run listens on BIOBANK_DEBUG off Django debug mode; never on a shared server

Optional feature flags in this profile are off: BIOBANK_HPC_ENABLED, BIOBANK_JUPYTER_ENABLED, BIOBANK_ONLINE_INTEGRATIONS_ENABLED.

docs.title: Institutional deployment (biobank.settings)
docs.text:
Variable Purpose SECRET_KEY, DEBUG, ALLOWED_HOSTS, DATABASE_URL Standard Django settings BIOBANK_MEDIA_ROOT, BIOBANK_STORAGE_ROOT Uploaded files and persistent storage roots BIOBANK_GROUP_ROOT, BIOBANK_INVENTORY_ROOT, BIOBANK_SAMPLE_DOCS_ROOT, BIOBANK_MANIFESTS_ROOT, BIOBANK_SHARED_ROOT Sub-folders of the storage root BIOBANK_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS Public https:// origins (comma-separated) BIOBANK_STORAGE_GLOBAL_ADMINS Usernames allowed to inspect every storage workspace (also need staff or superuser) BIOBANK_STORAGE_SUPERUSER_IS_GLOBAL_ADMIN true lets any superuser do so (always on in the local profile) BIOBANK_ELN_API_HOST Host name sent to the local ELN API socket; must be in ALLOWED_HOSTS BIOBANK_PUBLIC_URL Public address of the installation, sent to the geocoding service as contact information BIOBANK_PAM_* PAM sign-in behind Apache (see clusters) BIOBANK_JUPYTER_* Jupyter servers started through Slurm BIOBANK_REPOSITORY_ROOT, BIOBANK_TAXONOMY_DIR Shared reference-data folders BIOBANK_ZENODO_TOKEN, BIOBANK_ZENODO_API Publishing to Zenodo (sandbox by default)

See also production deployment.

docs.title: Reference data (taxonomy, GTDB, ICTV)
docs.text:
Organism lookups use local indexes so no web service is needed. Build them from the downloaded releases:

python manage.py build_taxonomy_index
python manage.py build_gtdb_index
python manage.py build_ictv_index

Without an index the fields still accept free text.

docs.title: Optional: clusters, Slurm and the DaVinci-style deployment
docs.text:
A local installation needs none of this. Everything below is optional and off by default.

Feature Local default What to set to enable it Sign-in Accounts in the application PAM behind Apache: use biobank.settings and the files in deploy/ Jupyter notebooks Not started by the server (use your own Jupyter and the read API, planned) BIOBANK_JUPYTER_* settings and a runner script; needs Slurm Reference indexes (taxonomy, GTDB, ICTV) Built on demand into the data folder BIOBANK_REPOSITORY_ROOT, BIOBANK_TAXONOMY_DIR to share a folder on a cluster Database SQLite BIOBANK_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... Web server Built-in (waitress + WhiteNoise) Gunicorn behind Apache/Nginx; see deploy/ and docs/operations/

The production profile used at CEPID B3 on the DaVinci cluster is biobank.settings; the local profile is biobank.standalone_settings. Both come from the same code base.

docs.title: Install and upgrade
docs.text: B3 LIMS needs Python 3.12 or newer (or Docker). It does not need a cluster, Slurm, PAM accounts or a separate web server.

docs.title: Option 1: pipx and the setup wizard
docs.text:
pipx install "git+https://github.com/leepusp/biobank.git"
biobank-local setup
biobank-local run

pipx keeps B3 LIMS in its own environment (pip install into a virtual environment works too). setup asks four questions:

  1. Data folder (default ~/.biobank-local): the database, uploaded files, backups and config.env live here. It is the only folder you need to back up.
  2. Database: SQLite (one file, best for one person or a small lab) or PostgreSQL (a lab server with many users).
  3. Administrator: user name, optional e-mail and a password of at least 8 characters.
  4. Network: whether other computers will open the installation, and the time zone.

To script it, use biobank-local setup --non-interactive --admin-user NAME --admin-password SECRET (--database-url, --allowed-hosts, --time-zone, --demo are also available).

docs.title: Option 2: Docker Compose
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/leepusp/biobank.git && cd biobank
BIOBANK_ADMIN_PASSWORD='choose-a-long-password' docker compose up -d

The first start creates the installation from environment variables; later starts only bring the database up to date. Data lives in the biobank-data volume. With PostgreSQL:

BIOBANK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=... BIOBANK_DATABASE_URL=postgres://biobank:biobank@db:5432/biobank \
  docker compose --profile postgres up -d

docs.title: Option 3: from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/leepusp/biobank.git && cd biobank
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
biobank-local setup

docs.title: Letting the rest of the lab use it
docs.text:
By default B3 LIMS listens on 127.0.0.1 (this computer only). To open it to your network:

biobank-local run --host 0.0.0.0

and, during setup (or in config.env), give the name people will type: BIOBANK_ALLOWED_HOSTS=biobank.mylab.example,192.168.1.20. If they reach it through an HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy, Nginx, Apache), also set BIOBANK_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://biobank.mylab.example. Use HTTPS whenever people sign in over a network you do not control.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
biobank-local backup                 # writes ~/.biobank-local/backups/biobank_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.tar.gz

The archive holds the database folder (SQLite), uploaded files and config.env. With PostgreSQL, also run pg_dump -Fc (the archive only notes this). To restore, unpack the archive over an empty data folder and run biobank-local doctor. Test a restore before you need it.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pipx upgrade biobank-lims            # or: git pull && pip install -e .   /   docker compose pull && up -d --build
biobank-local migrate                # updates the database; never touches accounts

Take a backup first.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to do biobank-local: command not found pipx ensurepath, then open a new terminal The page has no styling biobank-local migrate (it also collects the web files) Bad Request (400) from another computer add the name or address you typed to BIOBANK_ALLOWED_HOSTS in config.env and restart "CSRF verification failed" behind a proxy set BIOBANK_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to the public https:// address Anything else biobank-local doctor checks the settings, the database and the free disk space

docs.title: User guide
docs.text: A short tour of the modules. Every screenshot is from the fictional demo lab (biobank-local setup --demo).

docs.title: Samples
docs.text: Samples hold the identity of a biological item: ID, type (bacterium, phage, plasmid, other), organism, biosafety level, owner, research group, biobank and collections. Type-specific fields appear for the type you pick, and IDs get a prefix per type (BAC-, PHA-, PLA-, SMP-).

docs.title: Many samples at once: sample tables
docs.text: Open Samples > Import, choose a sample type and download its template (Excel or CSV). Columns are typed (numbers, dates, drop-down lists), an example sheet shows a filled row, and the file is checked when you upload it. A row with a problem shows an Edit button: fix it on screen and it is validated again, so you never have to re-upload.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Storage is organised in workspaces (yours, or a research group's) that contain locations: freezer, rack, box, shelf. A box can be a grid (rows and columns) or have named compartments.

  • When you register a sample, type the path (Freezer A > Rack 1 > Box 2) or pick the levels with the buttons. If the first level is new it becomes your workspace. When the last place has a drawing, click a free position on it.
  • To move a box or a sample, select it in the tree and choose the destination; you can move between workspaces if you manage both sides. Every move is recorded in History.

docs.title: Electronic lab notebook
docs.text: Entries (experiments, protocols, analyses) have rich text, steps, tables, attachments, tags and links to samples, reagents and molecular records. Signing an entry locks it; changes after that are amendments with a reason. Templates can be shared with your group.

docs.title: Molecular registry
docs.text: Register DNA, RNA, plasmids, primers and proteins. Drop a GenBank, SnapGene, FASTA, EMBL or ApE file on the page: the name, type and sequence come from the file, and nothing has to be typed. Each record has a map, features, ORFs, restriction digest, a primer Tm calculator with adjustable reaction conditions, alignments and, for proteins, 3D structure.

docs.title: Shipments and compliance
docs.text: Plan a shipment, generate the transport documents your institution asks for (MTA/TTM, sender and content declarations, GMO/CIBio notification), print package labels and record receipt.

docs.title: Calendar and history
docs.text: The Lab Calendar books equipment. History lists what was done to samples (entries, moves, changes); you see your own activity, and administrators see everything.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text: Access follows roles at three levels: biobank (owner, manager, editor, viewer), collection and research group. Samples are private until you share them or mark them public. Every file download and export checks permission.

docs.title: B3 ELN — parity checklist with eLabFTW
docs.text:
Source studied: elabftw/elabftw master e60e66b (2 Nov 2026), read for behaviour only. eLabFTW is AGPL-3.0: no code is copied; every feature below is reimplemented in Django. The client libraries eLabFTW builds on are permissively licensed and may be used directly:

Library Licence Used for TinyMCE 6.8.x (last MIT line) MIT main rich-text editor (menus, tables, templates) jspreadsheet-ce 5 MIT spreadsheet with formulas inside entries FullCalendar 6 MIT scheduler / Lab Calendar Ketcher 3 Apache-2.0 chemical structure editor 3Dmol.js 2 BSD-3 molecule / structure viewer jsoneditor 10 Apache-2.0 metadata JSON editor

B3-only modules stay where eLabFTW has no equivalent: Biobank inventory (samples, collections, shipments), Molecular Registry, Jupyter/Slurm, workflows/Galaxy, ENA/NCBI/Zenodo submission.

Status: ✅ done · 🟡 partial · ⬜ to do. Release = planned B3 Bench release.

The classic notebook page was retired in 2.1; old links redirect to the entry page. The separate "Private drafts" store was retired in 2.1.1: private work is an entry with visibility Private. Draft files already written to a user's home are left untouched.

docs.title: Eln hybrid architecture v1
docs.text: RETIRED (2.1.1). The private-drafts store described below no longer exists in the application. Private work is now an ELN entry with visibility Private. Kept for history.

docs.title: B3 LIMS — Hybrid ELN Architecture v1
Objective
docs.text:
Integrate the original eLabFTW experiment engine into the canonical B3 LIMS Django application while adopting the visual design references from the ELN kit.

The existing Django Notebook remains unchanged during the experimental phase.

docs.title: Sources of truth
docs.text:
• B3 LIMS / PostgreSQL: Samples, Storage, Chemicals, Molecular Registry, institutional permissions and cross-system links.
  • eLabFTW 6.0.9 / MySQL 8.4: Experiments, experiment templates, steps, revisions, comments, audit trails and native ELN attachments.

Do not duplicate eLabFTW experiment records as new NotebookEntry objects.

docs.title: Integration contract
docs.text:
• Use eLabFTW REST API v2.
  • Do not directly modify eLabFTW MySQL tables from Django.
  • Associate records through stable external identifiers.
  • Enforce Django-side authorization before API operations.
  • Preserve user attribution and eLabFTW team permissions.
  • Do not share one unrestricted user identity across researchers.
  • Do not expose database or API credentials to browsers.
  • Do not claim connectivity until an authenticated API call passes.

docs.title: User interface
docs.text:
• New Lab Tools > ELN Experimental menu item.
  • Existing Notebook stays visible and functional.
  • Page templates extend internal/common/base.html.
  • English labels and Bootstrap 5.3 conventions.
  • First screens: experiment list, detail and templates.
  • Kit HTML/PNG files are design references only.
  • No dynamic JavaScript evaluator from mockups.
  • The feature is disabled by default and restricted to explicitly authorized evaluators.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
• Original upstream eLabFTW version: 6.0.9.
  • MySQL: 8.4, database b3eln_poc.
  • Private rootless Podman network.
  • Persistent experimental storage: /home/public/apps/biobank/storage/eln-experimental
  • No externally published container ports.
  • No production data migrations.
  • Keep upstream source separate from the Django source.
  • Review AGPL-3.0 obligations before release.

docs.title: Delivery sequence
docs.text:
1. Preserve kit mockups and document the hybrid design.
  2. Implement feature gate, isolated URL, view and template.
  3. Test evaluator authorization and disabled behavior.
  4. Establish secure Django-to-eLabFTW API connectivity.
  5. Provision and map experimental identities.
  6. Implement read-only experiments and templates.
  7. Validate synthetic create/edit/revision workflows.
  8. Implement Biobank links to experiment identifiers.
  9. Complete backup, restore and resource-limit validation.
  10. Deploy through the existing production release workflow.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria for initial UI
docs.text:
• Existing Notebook unchanged.
  • Experimental URL inaccessible when disabled.
  • Unauthorized users cannot access experimental data.
  • No dependency on a running eLabFTW service for ordinary B3 LIMS routes or tests.
  • No new Django schema migration for the initial UI.
  • Existing tests remain green.
  • Validation uses only: https://davinci.icb.usp.br/b3lims

docs.title: Reference material
docs.text:
• docs/design/eln_kit_reference/
  • docs/development/eln_kit_roadmap_reference.md

The kit roadmap describes a Django-native backend approach. It is retained as a requirements reference, not as the implementation authority for this hybrid design.

docs.title: ELN roadmap: features adapted from eLabFTW
docs.text:
This is the working spec for extending the Biobank ELN, Lab Calendar and chemical tools with features found in eLabFTW. Each implementation step has an ID (for example 1.3) that pull requests and prompts refer to.

Mockups: docs/design/eln/ (open the HTML files in a browser).

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text:
1. No eLabFTW code. eLabFTW is AGPL-3.0. Use its repository only to read which entities, fields and rules exist. Never copy or translate its PHP, SQL, TypeScript or Twig into this repository. Write Django code from this spec.
  2. Third-party front-end libraries may be used directly when their licence allows it: FullCalendar core and the daygrid, timegrid, list and interaction plugins (MIT), Ketcher (Apache-2.0), jsoneditor (Apache-2.0), 3Dmol (BSD-3-Clause), OpenCloning (MIT, separate container). Do not use @fullcalendar/timeline or other FullCalendar premium plugins.
  3. Existing data is preserved. Every model change ships with a migration; value changes ship with a data migration that has a reverse function.
  4. Tests run on SQLite (biobank/test_settings.py). PostgreSQL-only features (exclusion constraints, btree_gist, RDKit) must be guarded by connection.vendor == "postgresql" and must also be enforced in Python.
  5. Permissions stay centralized in core/permissions/. Views never check ownership inline.
  6. Business logic lives in core/services/; views stay thin.
  7. English for code, templates, labels, messages and migration names.
  8. Before each pull request: python manage.py check, python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run, python manage.py test.

docs.title: Current state (before this roadmap)
docs.text:
• core/models/lab_tools/notebook.py: NotebookEntry with hard-coded ENTRY_TYPE_CHOICES, STATUS_CHOICES, VISIBILITY_CHOICES; NotebookBlock, NotebookAttachment, NotebookSampleLink, NotebookChemicalLink, NotebookMolecularLink, NotebookJupyterLink.
  • Templates are a Python dict in core/views/internal/lab_tools/notebook.py::_notebook_entry_templates().
  • notebook_delete_entry_api deletes rows permanently.
  • core/permissions/notebook.py: private / lab visibility; shared has no effect.
  • core/models/access_grants.py: generic ResourceAccessGrant (user or ResearchGroup, level view/edit/manage).
  • core/views/internal/calendar/views.py: lists the last 100 sample Events.
  • core/models/chemicals/chemical.py: Chemical mixes identity (name, CAS, formula) and stock (lot, quantity, location text).
  • core/models/samples/storage.py: StorageLocation tree and SampleStorageAssignment.

docs.title: 1.1 Categories and statuses
docs.text:
New models in core/models/lab_tools/notebook_settings.py:

  • NotebookCategory: research_group (FK, nullable = global), title, color (hex), custom_id_prefix (default EXP), is_private, ordering, is_active, timestamps. Unique (research_group, title) case-insensitive.
  • NotebookStatus: research_group, title, color, is_default, ordering, is_active, timestamps. One default per group.

NotebookEntry.category and NotebookEntry.status become FKs (on_delete=PROTECT, nullable during migration). A data migration creates global categories from the current ENTRY_TYPE_CHOICES and global statuses from STATUS_CHOICES, then maps every entry. The archived status becomes state=archived in step 1.2. Keep the old fields until the data migration runs, then remove them in a separate migration.

eLabFTW reference: tables experiments_categories, experiments_status.

docs.title: 1.2 Entry identity, state and locking
docs.text:
Add to NotebookEntry:

  • custom_id (positive int, nullable) and property display_id ({prefix}-{year}-{custom_id:03d}). Assigned on create: next number per category prefix and year, inside a transaction (select_for_update).
  • rating (0–5), content_type (html | markdown, default html).
  • state (normal | archived | deleted, indexed). Default managers return normal only; add all_objects.
  • locked, locked_by, locked_at; last_change_by.
  • created_from_template (FK to NotebookTemplate, nullable, added in 1.3).

Delete becomes state=deleted; add archive, unarchive and restore actions and a Trash filter. Locked entries reject edits except unlock by the locker, the owner or a group coordinator.

docs.title: 1.3 Templates as records
docs.text:
NotebookTemplate: title, description, icon (Bootstrap Icons name), owner, research_group, default_category, default_status, content, protocol_content, blocks_json (initial blocks), metadata (extra-field schema, used in 3.1), default_read_base, default_write_base, ordering, is_active, timestamps. Steps for templates come in 3.3.

Data migration: create one global template per entry in _notebook_entry_templates() (same keys, labels, icons, content). The create menu reads templates from the database; notebook_create?template=<id> copies fields into the new entry and sets created_from_template. Keep the helper function only as the seed source, or delete it once tests use the table.

docs.title: 1.4 Revisions, changelog and comments
docs.text:
• NotebookRevision: entry, content, protocol_content, content_type, created_by, created_at. Saved by a service when content changes and at most once per 5 minutes per user, plus always before lock and sign. Keep the last 100 per entry.
  • NotebookChangelog: entry, user, field, old_value, new_value, created_at. Written by the service for title, category, status, rating, permissions, lock state, links and steps.
  • NotebookComment: entry, author, body, is_immutable, timestamps.
  • Views: revision list and side-by-side compare; restore a revision (creates a new revision); comment create/delete (author only, not when immutable).

docs.title: 1.5 Read and write permissions
docs.text: Replace visibility with read_base and write_base (owner | group | institution) plus explicit ResourceAccessGrants for users and research groups. Migration: private → owner, lab → institution (current behaviour: any authenticated user), shared → owner. Rewrite visible_notebook_entries_for_user, can_view_notebook_entry and can_edit_notebook_entry; add can_manage_notebook_entry. Superusers keep full access. Permissions modal in the entry view.

docs.title: 1.6 Entry list (mockup 01-eln-entry-list)
docs.text: Scope tabs (mine / my groups / all readable), filters (category, status, owner, state, tags), search with simple key:value terms (category:, status:, tag:, owner:), pinned entries (NotebookPin: user + entry), steps progress, rating, integrity column, batch actions (status, tag, lock, archive, export). Paginate server side.

docs.title: 1.7 Entry view (mockup 02-eln-entry-view)
docs.text: Header with display ID, category, inline status select, rating, lock badge, tags; toolbar (edit, lock/unlock, duplicate, request signature, timestamp, permissions, export, pin); metadata row; right column with linked items, integrity card and Comments / Revisions / Changelog tabs. Existing blocks and attachments stay as they are.

docs.title: 2.1 Bookable equipment and bookings
docs.text:
core/models/scheduling/:

  • BookableResource: name, description, research_group, location (FK StorageLocation, nullable), color, is_bookable, max_minutes (0 = no limit), max_slots (open future bookings per user, 0 = no limit), can_overlap, users_can_book_in_past, is_cancellable, cancel_minutes, booking_window_days (0 = no limit), hourly_rate, currency, requires_note, is_active. Who can book uses ResourceAccessGrant (edit level = can book, manage = can manage).
  • Booking: resource, user, research_group, title, start, end, notebook_entry (nullable), recurrence_id (UUID, nullable), recurrence_index, recurrence_rule (JSON: frequency daily|weekly, interval, weekdays, count or until), cancelled_at, timestamps.
  • core/services/booking_rules.py: validate_booking(resource, user, start, end, exclude_ids=()) checks, in order: permission, end after start, past start, max_minutes, booking_window_days, max_slots, overlap. Returns every failed rule (the UI lists them). Recurring bookings expand to one row per occurrence and are validated as a whole.
  • PostgreSQL only: btree_gist + an exclusion constraint on (resource, tstzrange(start, end)) for non-overlapping resources, added with a vendor-guarded RunSQL.

docs.title: 2.2 Calendar UI (mockup 04-lab-calendar)
docs.text: Replace calendar_view. FullCalendar 6 (daygrid, timegrid, list, interaction) from a CDN already allowed by the project. JSON endpoints: list events in a range, create, move/resize, cancel, plus a validate endpoint used live by the booking form. Sample Events stay visible as a separate toggleable source. CSV export of bookings for a range.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Extra fields, builder, steps, links
3.1 Extra fields
docs.text:
Add metadata = JSONField(default=dict) to NotebookEntry (template already has it). Format, kept compatible with the .eln export of eLabFTW:

{
  "elabftw": {"extra_fields_groups": [{"id": 1, "name": "Culture conditions"}]},
  "extra_fields": {
    "Temperature (°C)": {"type": "number", "value": "28", "group_id": 1, "position": 3,

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Keep unpublished scientific data under the owning researcher's established project directory in their Unix home, while using the centralized eLabFTW service for explicitly published experiment versions.

docs.title: Private draft
docs.text:
• Source of truth: user's existing project directory.
  • Store experiment body, steps, revisions and attachments within the authorized project namespace.
  • Do not send draft contents to the central eLabFTW API.
  • Do not store draft contents in the central MySQL database.
  • Do not put scientific draft contents into shared logs.
  • Never derive a filesystem path directly from a URL or user-supplied project name.

docs.title: Shared project
docs.text:
• A shared project is not automatically public.
  • The authoritative project files remain in the authorized project directory.
  • Collaboration requires an explicit access policy.
  • Sharing must not trigger publication.

docs.title: Published version
docs.text:
• Publication is an explicit, authorized operation.
  • A validated snapshot is sent to the eLabFTW REST API.
  • The central eLabFTW database stores the published record.
  • Published attachments use institutional storage.
  • Publication preserves the private source.
  • Record source version, checksum, publication status, remote ID, author and publication timestamp.
  • Repeated submissions must not create duplicates.

docs.title: Filesystem integration
docs.text:
Reuse the existing Biobank user-home storage service and its privileged storage broker.

The final project-relative ELN namespace must be defined after verifying the existing project layout and the broker's supported operations.

Do not grant unrestricted home-directory access to apache or ladmin.

Never allow symlink traversal, path escape, cross-user access or direct arbitrary filesystem operations.

Use atomic writes, ownership verification and restrictive permissions. Failed saves must preserve existing data.

docs.title: Application integration
docs.text:
• Django enforces user and project authorization.
  • Private drafts use the user-home storage adapter.
  • Published records use eLabFTW REST API v2.
  • MySQL remains owned and managed by eLabFTW.
  • No direct Django writes to eLabFTW MySQL tables.
  • The existing Notebook is preserved unchanged.
  • The feature remains disabled until integration tests pass.

docs.title: Important limitation
docs.text:
A native eLabFTW private experiment is still stored in its configured MySQL database.

Therefore, central eLabFTW private permissions alone do not satisfy this storage policy.

Private editing functionality must be implemented against the user-home storage contract, or supported by another explicitly approved isolated architecture.

Do not claim the complete native eLabFTW editor works with home-only persistence before this is demonstrated.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Private save never calls the central eLabFTW API.
  • Private save never writes the central MySQL database.
  • Cross-user reads and writes are denied.
  • Path traversal and symlink escape are denied.
  • Existing project ownership is preserved.
  • Sharing does not publish.
  • Publishing requires explicit authorization.
  • Published content matches the approved source hash.
  • Failed publication preserves the private version.
  • No private content is exposed through a public index.
  • All existing Biobank tests continue to pass.

docs.title: Production requirements
docs.text:
Canonical repository: /home/ladmin/git/biobank

Canonical validation URL: https://davinci.icb.usp.br/b3lims

No alternate browser endpoint, localhost preview, or replacement of the existing Notebook.

No database migrations or deployment are authorized by this document alone.

docs.title: 6. ELN ideas from the references
docs.text:
Sources: Chemotion ELN (UI "Adjusting views", Details/Analyses, element model, LabIMotion), LabCollector ELN add-on. The B3 ELN already has: author signature with lock, amend and deviations (notebook_trace.py), revisions, templates stored in the database, backlinks to samples/reagents/molecules/Jupyter, sharing with groups, favourite tags, step groups, custom fields, Zenodo export. Ideas that are still missing:

From Chemotion: - [ ] Per-user list columns and detail tabs: drag items between "shown" and "available" (entries list, samples list, registry cards); stored in the user profile. - [ ] Collapsible side bars and a one-click full-screen detail window. - [ ] Analyses: entry or sample, then analyses, then datasets, then attachments; file conversions produce more attachments (spectra, chromatograms, gel images). Start with a generic "Analysis" block that groups files and metadata per measurement, with instrument and method fields. - [ ] Wellplate / screen element: a plate map (the storage grid drawing can be reused) with one Sample per well and results per well; screen = a set of plates. - [ ] Research plan: an entry type that mixes text, tables, images and links to other elements (we have blocks; add a plan template and a timeline). - [ ] Inbox: a folder where instrument files arrive (or are dropped) and are attached to entries later (Chemotion "Inbox", "folder collector"). - [ ] Generic modules builder (LabIMotion): define a new entry module with typed fields and publish it as a template; we have the field builder, extend it to repeatable groups and units. - [ ] Repository transfer: publish selected entries/datasets with metadata (JSON-LD, DOI through Zenodo); a review step before publishing. - [ ] History tracker for tables with variations (reaction variations); for us: per-cell history in entry tables.

From LabCollector: - [ ] Review and witness workflow: second signature with meaning (witnessed, reviewed, approved), signature certificate with name, title and role, searchable by those. - [ ] Duplicate a protocol page as a linked sub-page per batch (repeated assays such as ELISA), keeping the link to the parent protocol. - [ ] Template preview before use, and locked steps in validated templates. - [ ] Integrated spreadsheets with templates and a diagram designer (we have tables and Whiteboard-like artifacts; add a simple diagram block). - [ ] Report builder: compile several entries into one print/PDF, with the audit trail. - [ ] Data link: reference any LIMS record (sample, equipment, reagent) inside a page with a live card (done for samples; extend to equipment and storage positions, which is "hub, part 2" in the checklist). - [ ] Structure and substructure search in the chemical module (structure_search exists; expose it in the ELN).

docs.title: Storage review: behaviour and interface
docs.text: Date: 2026-11-04. Review only, no code changed. Screens checked in a dev database with one workspace, nine locations (room, two freezers, two shelves, rack, three boxes, two of them 9 x 9 grids) and 30 recorded samples.

docs.title: 1. What exists
docs.text:
Data model (core/models/samples/storage.py)

  • StorageWorkspace: ownership boundary, personal or research group.
  • StorageLocation: tree (room, freezer, shelf, rack, box, position, other), workspace optional (null = legacy unscoped inventory).
  • StorageLocationLayoutV8146C3: optional grid (rows x columns, max 26 x 24) with type and temperature labels.
  • SampleStorageAssignment: sample, location, free-text position, status; a unique active slot per (location, lower(position)).
  • StorageMovement + StorageMovementItem: audited moves of a container, a sample or a selection, with path snapshots.
  • StorageSceneConfiguration: per-user visual configuration (profiles per root) used only by the legacy interface.

Services: about 25 modules (storage_*), including movement preview and confirmation, subtree delete/unassign, workspace delete, writer lock, reconcile, legacy projection and sync. Permissions are workspace based.

Interface: /storage/ serves index_v814.html (canonical). ?legacy=1 serves index.html (the older Storage Designer). Both are in production.

docs.title: 2. Behaviour findings
docs.text:
1. Moves are safe by design: preview with before/after, a reason, one audited movement per operation, a lock for writers. Keep.
  2. A location stores only its parent, so moving a container moves everything below it. The interface says so ("0 locations and 12 Samples depend on this level"). Keep.
  3. Occupancy is only known for grid boxes. In the dev data the room card says "24/162 positions, 30 Samples": the 6 samples in a free box count as samples but not as occupied positions, so the ratio mixes two measures. Needs one rule (for example capacity shown only where every descendant box is a grid, otherwise show samples only).
  4. position is free text. The grid view assumes "A1" style names; names such as "a1" or "1A" are tolerated by the unique index (case-insensitive) but may not land on the grid. Needs a validation or a "not on the map" list.
  5. Historical registrations (legacy text locations) are shown read-only in every location view. Useful for audit, but they add noise to the main screen; they could move into a collapsed "Historical" section.
  6. Everything is delivered in one page: all visible locations and all visible assignments are embedded as <template> data and filtered in the browser. Fine for hundreds of samples, a problem for tens of thousands. No pagination, no server-side search (the search box was hidden in v8.14.7).
  7. Sample-to-storage links exist elsewhere (sample intake, bulk storage move, shipments, ELN is not linked yet). There is no storage container picker on an ELN entry (roadmap 2.3).

docs.title: 3. Interface findings
docs.text:
Canonical screen (v8.14), tabs Contents / Path tree / Movements / Manage.

  • Contents: tree on the left with sample counts, stats cards, child cards, list of recorded samples (collapsed for boxes), position map for grids. The position map is the best part: clear, shows occupancy, selectable.
  • Path tree: a horizontal graph of levels. With 5 levels the first two columns are cut off on a 1440 px screen ("zer -20 B"), and the "Level 5" label for a box counts the room as level 1, which is confusing for users.
  • Movements: empty table plus a collapsed "Sample transfers" block, two places for one idea (container moves vs sample moves).
  • Manage: long list with an inner scroll box and a second "Selected location" block below it, so the edit form is far from the list.
  • Overview (nothing selected): shows only the root as a card with the mixed occupancy figure; nothing visual for the freezer or rack level.

Legacy screen (?legacy=1), which is where the "illustration" lives (isometric blocks, 2D, hierarchy, graph, "Isometric + 2D" modes).

  • Shows "0 Samples" on the room and on both freezers because counts are not rolled up, while the new screen rolls them up (30).
  • Text overlaps at the bottom of the viewer and the Back button overlaps the level selector at 1440 px.
  • The user already moved the lab off the 3D viewer because it broke by browser; the SVG isometric replaced it but it still is a separate mode set.
  • About 6,900 lines of JS/CSS (14 scripts plus the explorer stylesheet) are loaded only by this screen, plus 2,068 lines of templates, plus the scene configuration model and services (about 680 lines). Tests still reference these files, which is why they cannot simply be deleted.

docs.title: 4. What the interface does not illustrate yet
docs.text:
• Freezer, shelf and rack levels have no picture: a user sees a list of child cards and a number. A rack could be shown as tiles (one per box) with a fill bar, a shelf as a row of racks, a freezer as its shelves.
  • No heat of occupancy across the whole tree (which freezers are nearly full).
  • No "find a free position" helper when registering or moving samples.
  • No label/printing support (box labels, QR) and no scan-to-locate.
  • No capacity warning when a box is full on registration.

docs.title: 5. Proposed decisions (to confirm)
docs.text:
Keep: the data model, movement flow and audit, the position grid, the tree with roll-up counts, workspaces and permissions.

Change in small releases:

  1. Define one occupancy rule and show it consistently (tree, cards, stats).
  2. Container view: tiles with fill bars for the children of the selected location, replacing the isometric and graph modes in the new screen.
  3. Path tree: fit levels in the viewport (scroll to the selected column, level numbers relative to the workspace root).
  4. Manage tab: put the edit form beside or above the list, move the historical registrations into a collapsed section.
  5. Server-side pagination and search for samples in a location (needed before the sample count grows).
  6. Free-position helper and capacity check in registration and moves.

Retire (after the above): the ?legacy=1 interface, its 14 scripts, templates, scene configuration model and services, with an expand/contract plan for the model and its tests. Do this last, once the lab confirms that nothing from the isometric view is still needed.

docs.title: 6. Questions for the lab
docs.text:
• Which view do people actually use today: legacy isometric, or only the new screen? (Production access logs can answer this.)
  • Do boxes always use A1-style grids, or are other position names in use?
  • Is label printing or scanning a requirement for this phase?

docs.title: Per-user Lab Tools storage
docs.text: Biobank keeps institutional inventory metadata and files in PostgreSQL and the shared application storage. Personal Lab Tools artifacts are isolated in the authenticated Linux user's home, following the deployment pattern used for Galaxy real-user storage.

docs.title: Ownership model
docs.text:
For a Linux user alice, the managed layout is:

/home/alice/biobank/lab_tools/
├── eln/entries/<entry-id>/attachments/
├── jupyter/notebooks/notebook_<notebook-id>/
├── jupyter/jobs/notebook_<notebook-id>/<run-id>/
├── molecular/records/                 # reserved for molecular file exports
├── exports/
└── tmp/

The user and their primary group own these directories and artifacts. Their mode is 0770 for directories and 0660 for files. A named ACL grants the trusted ladmin application account only the access required to serve and update the owner's data. No other user receives access.

PostgreSQL remains the source of truth for object identifiers, ownership, visibility, permissions, relationships, audit metadata, and Jupyter session state. Inventory/sample uploads remain under MEDIA_ROOT. ELN attachments and Jupyter files are never served directly by Apache; authenticated Django views enforce object permissions before opening them.

docs.title: Slurm identity
docs.text:
The web process does not impersonate a user directly. It invokes two narrowly scoped, root-owned helpers through sudo. The Jupyter helper validates the Linux account and every path, then invokes both sbatch and scancel through runuser as the notebook owner. Consequently, squeue and sacct show the real user and use that user's normal Slurm account and limits—not the shared biobank account.

Repository changes, Django checks, migrations, and application tests run as ladmin. Root is used only to install the reviewed helpers and sudo policy or to repair ownership and ACLs. During a normal launch, Django runs as ladmin, the root-owned helper validates the request, and sbatch runs as the notebook owner through runuser.

docs.title: Jupyter node and resource selection
docs.text:
The launch form defaults to Automatic (Slurm decides). A user may instead request one allowlisted compute node: n01, gn01, gn02, or gn03. The selection is validated by the Django view, the Jupyter service, and the root-owned runner. The runner omits --nodelist for automatic placement and adds exactly one validated --nodelist=NODE argument for an explicit choice.

The application and runner share these limits:

  • 1–128 CPU cores;
  • 1024–1048576 MB of memory;
  • basic: 1–72 hours;
  • max50: 1–168 hours.

Slurm remains authoritative for current node state, available resources, and partition policy.

docs.title: Managed JupyterLab
docs.text:
A running Biobank notebook exposes Open JupyterLab. The Notebook and JupyterLab interfaces use the same authenticated Slurm allocation, Jupyter server, protected node proxy, token and persistent workspace. Opening JupyterLab does not submit another job.

The managed server exposes only the authenticated Linux user's home as its file-browser root. It opens initially at biobank/lab_tools/jupyter/notebooks/notebook_<id>/notebook.ipynb. The /workspace path remains an alias for that notebook workspace.

When the managed session is stopped, the page offers only Start managed session. There is no link to a separate Open OnDemand JupyterLab.

The managed JupyterLab URL must use the protected Biobank node proxy. It must never link directly to a compute-node port.

docs.title: Runtime artifact retention
docs.text:
jupyter/notebooks/notebook_<id>/ is persistent user data.

jupyter/jobs/notebook_<id>/<run_id>/ is transient control data. It may contain the generated submission script, Slurm output, connection metadata and isolated Jupyter runtime directories.

The protected runner removes a run directory after a terminal status, an owner-scoped stop, a failed submission, or an explicit protected session-cleanup. Persistent notebook workspaces are not removed by session cleanup.

Although $HOME is the authenticated user's real /home/<username>, Jupyter runtime, configuration, data, cache, Matplotlib and IPython paths are redirected to /runtime. These artifacts remain transient and are removed with the session run directory.

docs.title: Deployment order
docs.text:
1. Back up PostgreSQL, the Git candidate, the current Biobank application storage, the current Jupyter runner, and the applicable sudoers files.
  2. Confirm there are no active legacy Biobank Jupyter jobs. Stop them through the application before changing the runner.
  3. Have an administrator run deploy/install_lab_tools_home_storage.sh from the reviewed release tree. This is the only step requiring unrestricted root access. It installs the reviewed sandbox runtime under /home/public/apps/biobank/runtime/notebook_server.sh, a root-controlled path shared with every compute node. The application root uses mode 2771, the shared runtime directory uses 0751, and notebook_server.sh uses 0755. This gives authenticated Slurm users execute-only pathname traversal to the shared runtime without granting membership in the biobank Unix group or access to protected application directories such as storage, backups, and logs. A head-node-only path such as /usr/local/libexec must not be written into Slurm job scripts. Installation accepts only the reviewed isolated-runtime SHA-256 2e9144ff1591509eb8c8912d0ce655fac9434f7584ab217afd84f6160b2784a1 or the current authenticated-home runtime SHA-256 9a576f69972add1e9a455e425964be9d4ab711fc734b66eec37fdf622f31ad0f.
  4. Set BIOBANK_LAB_TOOLS_PROVISION_ON_LOGIN=1 in the protected Biobank service environment, deploy the Django source, then run:
/home/public/conda/envs/biobank/bin/python manage.py check
/home/public/conda/envs/biobank/bin/python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
/home/public/conda/envs/biobank/bin/python manage.py migrate
  1. Preview and apply legacy ELN attachment copies:
/home/public/conda/envs/biobank/bin/python manage.py migrate_lab_tools_attachments
/home/public/conda/envs/biobank/bin/python manage.py migrate_lab_tools_attachments --apply

Keep the shared sources until backup and user acceptance are complete. Only then rerun with --apply --delete-source if removal is explicitly approved.

  1. Restart biobank.service, log in as two different real users, and create one ELN attachment and one Jupyter notebook for each user.
  2. Validate ownership and isolation:
namei -l /home/USER/biobank/lab_tools
getfacl -p /home/USER/biobank/lab_tools
find /home/USER/biobank/lab_tools -maxdepth 5 -printf '%M %u:%g %p\n'
squeue -o '%.18i %.12u %.20j %.10T'

For Jupyter, test both automatic placement and one explicit node. Confirm that the job owner is the authenticated Linux user and that the selected node appears in squeue after allocation.

The runner automatically copies an old notebook workspace from the exact legacy user_<django-id>_<username>/notebook_<id> directory the first time that notebook is started. It does not delete the old workspace.

Migration 0066 changes only the Django storage declaration and field length; legacy attachment names remain readable, so rolling back does not require moving files immediately. Do not delete per-user or legacy data during rollback.

docs.title: Production deployment, backups and governance
docs.text: This page keeps the operational guidance that used to be in the README. It applies to a server that other people rely on (the institutional profile biobank.settings, or biobank-local on a lab server).

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose SECRET_KEY Django cryptographic signing key DEBUG Enables or disables Django debug mode ALLOWED_HOSTS Comma-separated allowed host names DATABASE_URL Django database connection URL BIOBANK_MEDIA_ROOT Uploaded-file root BIOBANK_STORAGE_ROOT Root for persistent institutional storage BIOBANK_NOTEBOOK_STORAGE_MODE Notebook storage strategy BIOBANK_NOTEBOOK_ROOT Notebook artifact root BIOBANK_GROUP_ROOT Research-group storage root BIOBANK_INVENTORY_ROOT Inventory artifact root BIOBANK_SAMPLE_DOCS_ROOT Sample-document root BIOBANK_MANIFESTS_ROOT Generated manifest root BIOBANK_SHARED_ROOT Shared artifact root

Use absolute, access-controlled paths in production. Values in .env.example are development examples only.

docs.title: Static and persistent files
docs.text:
Source templates and static assets live under core/interfaces/ and static/. Build collected assets with:

python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

The generated staticfiles/ directory must not be committed.

Uploaded sample files, notebook attachments, shipment documents, signed documents, and import files are persistent data. They must:

  • live outside the Git repository in production;
  • use restrictive ownership and permissions;
  • be backed up independently from PostgreSQL;
  • be served only through an authorization-aware mechanism;
  • never be exposed by an unrestricted static-file alias.

Database backups do not include uploaded files.

docs.title: Permissions and data governance
docs.text:
Authorization logic is centralized under core/permissions/. Supported workflows include biobank-level and collection-level roles, ownership, research-group membership, superuser administration, and visibility filtering.

New views, downloads, exports, and file-serving endpoints must apply the appropriate permission helper. Hiding a link in a template is not an authorization control.

Do not add real sample records, patient or participant information, scientific metadata, user lists, shipment documents, signed forms, credentials, or database dumps to fixtures, tests, screenshots, issues, or commits.

docs.title: Production deployment
docs.text:
A production installation should provide:

  1. a dedicated application account and group;
  2. an isolated Python environment;
  3. a PostgreSQL database and restricted database role;
  4. an environment file readable only by the application service;
  5. persistent file storage outside the source checkout;
  6. Gunicorn or another supported WSGI server;
  7. a TLS-enabled reverse proxy;
  8. collected static assets;
  9. authorization-aware delivery of protected uploads;
  10. separate, verified backups for PostgreSQL and persistent files.

Typical deployment validation:

python manage.py check
python manage.py check --deploy
python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
python manage.py migrate --plan
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

Review migration plans and back up PostgreSQL and persistent files before applying production schema changes. Deployment-specific hostnames, IP addresses, users, paths, service definitions, authentication providers, and backup schedules belong in private operational documentation.

docs.title: Backup and restore principles
docs.text:
PostgreSQL should be backed up with pg_dump in custom format. Persistent files require a separate filesystem-level backup. Each backup should have an integrity checksum and a retention policy.

A restore must first be tested against a temporary database and temporary file root. Database and file backups should be selected from compatible points in time. Stop write traffic and obtain explicit operational approval before a production restore.

See docs/operations/ for generic implementation guidance.

docs.title: Development workflow
docs.text:
Create focused branches from the current main branch:

git fetch origin --prune
git switch main
git pull --ff-only
git switch -c feature/short-description

Before opening a pull request:

python manage.py check
python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
python manage.py test
git status --short

Keep commits focused. Do not combine generated runtime data, local backups, or unrelated production changes with application code.
